summary: Added Tidebound’s persistent voyage library with named snapshots, learning notes, search and pagination, metadata edits, explicit snapshot replacement, archive/restore, confirmed deletion and game JSON export.

Replaced overwrite-only save slots with atomic IndexedDB metadata/snapshot transactions, expected revisions, cross-tab conflict protection, preserved legacy saves, retained drafts and commit-before-load/import/new-game behavior.
Fixed demolition refunds that consumed existing inventory when a paused warehouse left an island over capacity; corrected paused-warehouse capacity handling and preserved the final paused harbor.
Pinned dependencies, updated Vitest to the patched 4.1.11 release, added 21 focused regressions, and added a production-browser library runner that owns its local preview and isolated synthetic data.
Added nine detailed junior-to-mid-level guides, 42 exact original text snapshots, reviewed screenshots, real worked fixes, failure analysis, progressive CRUD exercises and review guidance.

checks.environment: Node 22.16.0; npm 10.9.2 clean install; Vite 7.3.6; Vitest 4.1.11; real Chrome 152.0.7977.76; isolated browser contexts
checks.command: 44 unit/domain tests; 19 production library workflows; 13 original gameplay workflows; normal clean install/build; byte-identical assets; npm audit; release and performance scripts

unitTests: does not consume inventory as a negative refund when a paused warehouse leaves the island over capacity
removes a paused warehouse without pretending it removes another 600 units of capacity
still protects the last harbor even when that harbor is paused
world and construction generates a deterministic complete archipelago and valid initial save
world and construction charges construction once and rejects occupancy, water, locked and non-coastal placement
world and construction protects required harbor and full warehouses when demolishing
economy and progression converts inputs exactly and stops when input runs out
economy and progression limits output by workforce and honors pause toggles
economy and progression stops production at storage capacity and explains it
economy and progression consumes food and luxury goods and reacts to starvation
economy and progression enforces research prerequisites and no duplicate purchases
economy and progression validates trades atomically and uses real resources and gold
economy and progression requires exploration, navigation and an expedition before settlement
shipping and persistence accepts the previously exported earned late-game fixture
shipping and persistence rejects unsafe identifier strings even when their references are internally consistent
shipping and persistence requires the original settled home island first with a valid coastal harbor
shipping and persistence shows paused fleet status without advancing a paused route
shipping and persistence partially unloads without losing overflow cargo
shipping and persistence does not award delivery progress for an empty ship
shipping and persistence saves paused harbors and resumes their waiting routes
shipping and persistence conserves cargo across repeated trips between player ports, even when a destination is full
shipping and persistence keeps ships outside the island shoreline throughout the sea journey
shipping and persistence restores routes, economy, events and deterministic continuation exactly
shipping and persistence rejects malformed, incompatible and broken-reference saves
shipping and persistence reaches a verified victory state when every independent objective is fulfilled
wins from a genuine new game using earned resources and public actions within 90 simulated minutes
voyage records and snapshots creates a normalized title and an exact independent snapshot
voyage records and snapshots edits details without changing the snapshot or its saved timestamp
voyage records and snapshots replaces only the snapshot and summary while preserving identity and notes
voyage records and snapshots returns a missing result instead of an empty or new world
voyage records and snapshots rejects malformed imports before creating any record or payload
voyage records and snapshots bounds input and uses UTF-8 bytes rather than JavaScript character count
concurrency and atomic outcomes allows only one concurrent creator with the same normalized title
concurrency and atomic outcomes allows exactly one writer of a shared expected revision
concurrency and atomic outcomes does not change metadata or payload after a stale replacement
concurrency and atomic outcomes rolls back an earlier metadata put when the payload write throws
concurrency and atomic outcomes preserves the previous world and revision after a failed replacement
concurrency and atomic outcomes protects reserved slots and prevents cross-tab slot overwrites
concurrency and atomic outcomes keeps an existing manual slot when another page tries initial legacy adoption
archive and delete lifecycle requires archive and removes metadata and snapshot together
archive and delete lifecycle cannot delete using an archive view after another tab restores the record
archive and delete lifecycle retains archived titles and forbids replacing archived snapshots
archive and delete lifecycle prevents a stale edit from recreating a deleted identity
archive and delete lifecycle enforces the collection cap inside competing creation transactions
libraryWorkflows: Create a named checkpoint and render markup-like learning notes as literal text
Edit metadata with stable identity and an incremented revision
Reject a duplicate normalized title and retain the editor draft
Search notes and show an explicit empty result
Export the exact saved world after a metadata edit
Retain the library after a full page reload
Protect a real two-tab edit and retain the losing draft for review
Reject a stale manual-slot save from a second page
Confirm snapshot replacement while preserving the title and notes
Archive and restore without losing the snapshot or allowing archived replacement
Cancel deletion safely, then permanently delete an archived checkpoint
Render a usable narrow library and navigate its editor by keyboard
Load a manual save and then a checkpoint through explicit confirmation
Reject invalid import, cancel valid import, then commit and reload a confirmed import
Paginate a collection larger than one page and bound navigation
Copy valid legacy slots without changing or deleting their original keys
Preserve malformed legacy autosave bytes and recover through the valid manual slot
Keep the game and export available when IndexedDB cannot open
Roll back a real-browser payload failure, retain the draft, and save after recovery
gameplayWorkflows: New game renders an interactive WebGL world and working initial settlement
Cottage placement on the 3D island consumes materials and adds residents
Farm placement, inspection and production pause/resume work
Research spends knowledge and unlocks a functional sawmill
NPC market screen buys and sells home-harbor goods with correct accounting
Two-way cargo route creation and pause/resume work through the interface
Exploration reveals new land and settlement correctly requires navigation
Manual saves, automatic reload and audio/motion settings survive reload
Export and import restore game state; malformed imports leave the active voyage intact
Keyboard pause/resume and in-game help work
390px mobile layout fits, and management screens remain usable
New-voyage confirmation can be cancelled; a new seed preserves the manual save
Standalone production build journal renders, filters tasks and exposes evidence

limits: Browser-local single-player application: no backend, accounts, server authorization, multi-tenancy or cloud synchronization. Collections are origin-specific and may be cleared or evicted.
Game JSON exports contain the saved world, not checkpoint titles or learning notes. Periodic and visibility-change saves do not guarantee completion during browser shutdown.

The original documented route-reassignment teleport simplification remains. This pass focuses on durable CRUD learning and the verified demolition accounting bug; it does not turn the simulation into a multiplayer service.

76 counted cases comprise 44 unit/domain tests, 19 library browser workflows and 13 original gameplay workflows. Clean setup, build, audit, release checks, the source comparison and performance measurements are additional evidence, not inflated into this case count.
Browser evidence is from Chrome 152.0.7977.76 on this Windows machine. Five-second graphics measurements are hardware-specific; the 101-building scene remains below 30 FPS in this run.

Original canonical generated artifacts are preserved. New verification logs and additional gameplay captures remain in the central checks directory; two reviewed library screenshots and the consolidated evidence are included with the course.
